# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish a visual codebook for Deaf, who can then describe the gestures aloud to Blind. I will use three distinct gestures in the manual’s row order: green, red, yellow; followed by the corresponding cut-wire gestures: red, yellow, green. Deaf can relay the gesture descriptions, and Blind can use the ordered pairs to apply the mapping to the observed light.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "👎", "👌", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile findings yet. Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position is safe, including any conditions. Also tell the Deaf that my next gesture means: report every visible display, light, colour, and marking on the bomb to you, then relay that report to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, and WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Blind sent me the gesture 🫵.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. Among the visible wires, red is position 3. Blind’s gesture is a request for Deaf to report the bomb’s complete visible state to him; I will signal that request and encode “red, three” using the established red sign repeated three times.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👎", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRE 1 yellow, WIRE 2 green, WIRE 3 red. Please use the manual to determine the exact safe wire position.

The green light requires cutting the red wire. The red wire is position 3, so I will signal three red-code gestures to Deaf; Deaf can relay that to Blind using the established code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instruction and name the safe wire position as a number: 1, 2, or 3. I cannot interpret gestures.

I cannot speak directly, so I must signal Deaf. The green light maps to cutting the red wire, which is wire position 3. Using the established code, I will send red followed by three position marks; Deaf can state the exact instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: We need a code. From now on, thumbs-down repeated 1 time means safe wire 1, 2 times means safe wire 2, and 3 times means safe wire 3. Please repeat the manual's safe wire using exactly that number of thumbs-down gestures.

The green light requires cutting the red wire, which is wire 3. Blind has defined repeated thumbs-down gestures as the wire-position code, so I will send exactly three thumbs-down gestures to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture sequence is not the agreed code because it includes fists. Speak the safe wire number plainly: say exactly wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Please give Blind the manual instruction by speech; I can only see your gestures.

I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot hear me; I can only communicate this to Deaf by gesture. The manual says green light means cut the red wire, which is wire 3. Under Blind’s agreed code, I will send exactly three thumbs-down gestures so Deaf can say “wire 3” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see gestures. Speak the answer now as exactly one number: 1, 2, or 3, for the safe wire position.

I cannot speak to Blind, but Deaf can see my gesture and relay the answer aloud. The green light requires the red wire, which is wire 3, so I will use the agreed three thumbs-down code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
```
